analyst_view.overall: PSG are top of the league phase with 12 points from 4 games after beating Nice 3-2; Roma are 20th with 4 points and need results, though they are second in Serie A and won 5-1 at Parma, with Malen in prolific form. PSG are without Doue and Kvaratskhelia (both knee ligament injuries; the numbers count both), while Dembele, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes are back and French reports have Dembele starting with Mayulu or Ferran Torres alongside. Roma's 21-man squad includes Balerdi, who passed a late fitness test although the numbers treat him as out, but previews have Mancini, N'Dicka and Hermoso in the back three; Pellegrini and Rensch are out. Swedish referee Glenn Nyberg (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted. This refresh found nothing big the numbers can't see, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, lifted by both teams' scoring form (about +6% PSG, +4% Roma) and with Doue (-6%) and Kvaratskhelia (-4%) already taken off PSG. Balerdi is back in Roma's squad, which the numbers didn't expect, but he looks set for the bench, and Dembele starting and Malen and Dybala or Soule for Roma fit the numbers' picture, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Roma's busy recent corner count already adding about 3%. PSG should have most of the ball and Gasperini's Roma go wide through wing-backs Wesley and Molina, both expected to start, but nothing in the team news changes how many corners either side wins, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already cut about 10% for referee Glenn Nyberg's low card count and for both sides' quiet recent records (PSG only 3 in their last 6). Roma's man-to-man pressing tends to draw fouls against a side that keeps the ball, which is why Roma carry the larger share; with no rivalry or suspension angle, I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots, with both sides' high recent shot counts already adding 9-11%. Losing Doue costs PSG a shooter, but Dembele is back to take that role and PSG should dominate the ball at home, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 13.1 shots on target, pushed up by PSG's very accurate recent run (+22%). Doue and Kvaratskhelia are already counted, and neither Svilar in Roma's goal nor Balerdi's return to the squad changes how many shots reach the goal by enough to move, so I stay at 13.1.
